notes: THE LOAD-BEARING CASE FOR A1. The hold lapses between create_checkout and complete_checkout, but the slot itself is still free. A naive implementation charges first and discovers the stale hold afterwards, leaving a charged buyer with no booking. A1 requires the availability re-check before the PSP call, and the hold/slot split requires hold_expired rather than slot_unavailable so the platform knows it can re-hold the same slot instead of sending the buyer back to slot selection.

when.notes: TTL elapses. The business releases the hold and restores capacity.remaining to 1. No other buyer takes the slot.

then.retry_guidance: Re-hold slot_20260316_1400 and repeat complete_checkout. Re-querying availability is not required, because the slot never became unavailable.

wrong_answers.behaviour: charge the PSP, then fail the booking write
wrong_answers.why: The buyer is charged for a booking that does not exist.
Tells the platform to discard a slot that is still bookable, costing the buyer their preferred time for no reason.

wrong_answers.behaviour: honour the expired hold and book anyway
wrong_answers.why: Capacity was already returned to the pool; another buyer may have been offered the same slot.
